gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the missing word or form to complete each cleft sentence. Twenty original sentences with it-clefts, wh-clefts and thing-clefts.

questions.after: found the missing keys.
questions.explain: Focus on the subject, a person: It + was + Maria + who / that + verb.

questions.after: decides the exam dates.
questions.explain: The focus is the person who does the action, so who or that introduces the verb ‘decides’.

questions.after: she bought, not the red one.
questions.explain: Focus on the object, a thing: It + was + the blue jacket + that + she bought.

questions.after: last Friday that we finally met.
questions.explain: The meeting is finished, so ‘be’ is past: It was last Friday that we met.

questions.after: I grew up.
questions.explain: Focus on a place: It is + in Girona + that (or where) + clause.

questions.before: It was because of the storm
questions.after: the match stopped.
questions.explain: Focus on the reason: It was + because of the storm + that + clause.

questions.after: the money that mattered to her.
questions.explain: The negative goes on ‘be’. ‘Last year’ is past, so: it wasn’t the money that mattered.

questions.after: midnight that the noise stopped.
questions.explain: The pattern is It wasn’t until + time + that + clause.

questions.after: it Maria who called you last night?
questions.explain: The question form puts ‘be’ first: Was it Maria who…? ‘Last night’ is past, so ‘was’.

questions.after: I need most right now is a long holiday.
questions.explain: A wh-cleft starts with ‘What’ + clause, then be, then the focus.

questions.after: his calm reaction.
questions.explain: The what-clause is followed by ‘be’. The surprise happened in the past, so ‘was’.

questions.after: the police.
questions.explain: After ‘what she did was’ use the base verb (or to + base verb): call, phone…

questions.before: What I want to do is
questions.after: the world for a whole year.
questions.explain: The focus is an action, so use the base verb (or to + base verb): travel, see…

questions.after: we stayed in Paris was a tiny hotel near the river.
questions.explain: The focus is a place (a tiny hotel near the river), so the cleft clause starts with ‘Where’.

questions.after: he left the company was that the pay was far too low.
questions.explain: The focus gives the reason (the pay was too low), so the cleft clause starts with ‘Why’.

questions.after: she won the match was by staying calm under pressure.
questions.explain: The focus gives the way she did it (by staying calm), so the cleft clause starts with ‘How’.

questions.after: I need.
questions.explain: In a reverse wh-cleft the focus comes first, then ‘is what’ + clause.

questions.after: that the website is far too slow.
questions.explain: In a thing-cleft, ‘be’ links the noun (problem) to the that-clause. The problem exists now, so ‘is’.

questions.after: I want is some peace and quiet.
questions.explain: A thing-cleft opens with a noun such as ‘thing’: The only thing I want is…

questions.after: many people never vote.
questions.explain: After ‘the fact is’, the that-clause gives the information.

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each cleft sentence — 20 examples with it-clefts, wh-clefts and thing-clefts. Some sentences can be built in more than one correct order.

matching.title: Match the plain sentence and its cleft
matching.subtitle: Tap a plain sentence, then tap the cleft sentence that gives the same information with a focus.

pairs.right: It was Maria who found the keys.
It was in Girona that we met.

pairs.left: Tom lost his phone on Monday.
pairs.right: It was on Monday that Tom lost his phone.
It was the noise that woke the baby.

pairs.left: She stayed in because of the storm.
pairs.right: It was because of the storm that she stayed in.
It was our teacher who chose the film.
It wasn’t the money that mattered.

pairs.left: The storm didn’t stop until midnight.
pairs.right: It wasn’t until midnight that the storm stopped.
What I need is a holiday.
What she did was call the police.
What surprised me was his reaction.

pairs.left: The team wants a new coach.
pairs.right: What the team wants is a new coach.
Where she went is a mystery.

pairs.left: Nobody explained how they did it.
pairs.right: How they did it was never explained.
The noise is what annoys her.
The problem is that the website is too slow.
The trouble is that we have no time.
The only thing I want is some peace.
The thing that worries me most is the exams.
The sad fact is that many people never vote.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Check what is being emphasised, and watch the linking words and the verb forms.

questions.text: It        Anna who broke the window, not Ben.
wrongReasons: ‘It’ doesn’t change, and ‘were’ doesn’t agree with ‘it’.
‘Did’ can’t be the verb ‘be’ in an it-cleft.
‘Has’ is not the verb ‘be’, which every it-cleft needs.
questions.explain: An it-cleft needs ‘be’ after ‘it’. The window was broken in the past: It was Anna who…

questions.text: It was the keys        she lost, not her wallet.
wrongReasons: ‘What’ can’t follow a noun focus like ‘the keys’.
‘Where’ is for places, and ‘the keys’ is a thing.
‘Whose’ shows possession, which isn’t the meaning here.
questions.explain: After a thing in focus, ‘that’ introduces the rest of the sentence.

questions.text: It was the price        put people off, not the quality.
wrongReasons: ‘Who’ is for people, but the price is a thing.
‘Where’ is for places, but the price is a thing.
‘What’ can’t follow a noun focus like ‘the price’.
questions.explain: After a thing in focus, ‘that’ links it to the verb ‘put’.

questions.text: It was in Barcelona        they first met.
wrongReasons: ‘Who’ is for people, and ‘in Barcelona’ is a place.
‘What’ doesn’t link a place focus to the clause.
‘Whom’ is for people, and ‘in Barcelona’ is a place.
questions.explain: For places, times and reasons, the linking word is ‘that’.

questions.text: It wasn’t        midnight that the music stopped.
wrongReasons: ‘Since’ would need a starting point in a present perfect sentence.
‘During’ doesn’t fit the pattern ‘It wasn’t… that’.
‘While’ is a conjunction and can’t come before ‘midnight’.
questions.explain: The fixed pattern is It wasn’t until + time + that + clause.

questions.text: I need is a long holiday.
wrongReasons: ‘That’ can’t be the subject in this wh-cleft.
‘Which’ needs a choice of things, but nothing is given.
‘It’ needs a ‘that’ or ‘who’ clause after the focus.
questions.explain: A wh-cleft starts with ‘What’ + clause, then be, then the focus.

questions.text: What surprised everyone        his reaction.
wrongReasons: ‘Were’ doesn’t agree with ‘what surprised everyone’, which is singular.
‘Did’ can’t link the clause to the focus.
‘Has’ can’t link the clause to the focus.
questions.explain: After the what-clause you need ‘be’. The surprise was in the past: was.

questions.text: What he did        walk out of the meeting.
wrongReasons: ‘Were’ doesn’t agree with the singular ‘what he did’.
‘Does’ is not the linking verb ‘be’.
‘Had’ is not the linking verb ‘be’.
questions.explain: ‘What he did’ is in the past, so the verb ‘be’ is ‘was’, followed by the base verb ‘walk’.

questions.text: What she did was        the police.
wrongReasons: After ‘what she did was’, we don’t repeat the past form.
The verb has no -s here; it is a base verb.
A present perfect form can’t follow ‘what she did was’.
questions.explain: After ‘what… did was’, use the base verb (or to + base verb).

questions.text: we stayed in Paris was a tiny hotel near the river.
wrongReasons: ‘What’ doesn’t fit: we stayed in a place, so the clause needs ‘where’.
‘Why’ would ask for a reason, but the focus is a place.
‘Who’ would ask for a person, but the focus is a place.
questions.explain: The focus (a tiny hotel near the river) is a place, so the cleft clause starts with ‘Where’.

questions.text: she won the match was by staying calm under pressure.
wrongReasons: ‘What she won the match’ is not a possible clause here.
‘Where’ would ask for a place, but the focus is a way of doing something.
‘Who’ would ask for a person, but the focus is a way of doing something.
questions.explain: The focus (by staying calm) is a way of doing something, so the cleft clause starts with ‘How’.

questions.text: The noise is        annoys her.
wrongReasons: ‘That’ can’t introduce a reverse wh-cleft here; the sentence needs ‘what’.
‘Who’ is for people, but the noise is a thing.
‘Where’ is for places, but the noise is a thing.
questions.explain: A reverse wh-cleft has the structure focus + is + what + clause.

questions.text: The problem        that the website is too slow.
wrongReasons: ‘Are’ doesn’t agree with the singular ‘the problem’.
‘Does’ can’t link the noun and the that-clause.
‘Has’ can’t link the noun and the that-clause.
questions.explain: In a thing-cleft, ‘be’ links the noun (problem) and the that-clause.

questions.text: The only thing I want right now        some peace and quiet.
wrongReasons: ‘Are’ doesn’t agree with ‘the only thing’, which is singular.
‘Does’ can’t link the noun phrase and the focus.
‘Was’ is past, but ‘want’ is present.
questions.explain: ‘The only thing I want’ is singular and present, so the linking verb is ‘is’.

questions.text: it Maria who called you last night?
wrongReasons: ‘Did’ can’t be followed by ‘it Maria who’ in a cleft question.
‘Has’ is not the verb ‘be’.
‘Does’ is present, but the call was last night.
questions.explain: A cleft question puts ‘be’ first: Was it Maria who…?

questions.text: It        the money that mattered; it was the people.
wrongReasons: ‘Didn’t’ can’t be followed by ‘the money that mattered’ in this pattern.
‘Hadn’t’ would be past perfect, which does not fit.
‘Weren’t’ doesn’t agree with ‘it’.
questions.explain: The negative goes on ‘be’: It wasn’t the money that mattered.

questions.text: It was        the storm that the match stopped.
wrongReasons: ‘Because’ needs a full clause, but ‘the storm’ is a noun phrase.
‘Although’ shows contrast, not a reason.
‘So’ can’t come before a noun phrase.
questions.explain: Before a noun phrase, use ‘because of’: It was because of the storm that…

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
choices: Was Tom who broke the vase.
It was Tom who broke the vase.
It were Tom who broke the vase.
It was Tom who he broke the vase.
wrongReasons: An it-cleft can’t leave out ‘it’.
‘It’ is singular, so ‘were’ is wrong.
The subject can’t be repeated: ‘who he’ is wrong.
questions.explain: It + was + focus + who + verb, with no repeated subject.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
choices: What I really love the music.
What I really love it is the music.
What I really love is the music.
What I really love are the music.
wrongReasons: The verb ‘be’ is missing.
You can’t add ‘it’ after the what-clause.
‘Are’ doesn’t agree with ‘the music’, which is singular.
questions.explain: What + clause + is + focus, with no extra words.

questions.text: Which sentence is more suitable for a formal report?
choices: The survey shows costs are rising, you know.
Costs are rising and stuff, the survey says.
What this survey shows is that costs are rising.
wrongReasons: ‘You know’ is a spoken filler and doesn’t belong in a formal report.
‘And stuff’ is too vague and informal for a report.
It is too short and incomplete for a formal report.
questions.explain: A wh-cleft with a clear subject suits formal reports and speeches.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong (if a word is missing, tap the word right after the gap). Twenty original sentences.

items.message: An it-cleft needs ‘it’: It was Maria who called.
‘It’ is singular: It was the students who complained.
‘Who’ is for people. For a thing use ‘that’: It was the keys that she lost.
Use ‘who’ or ‘that’ after a person, not ‘what’: It was Anna who broke the window.
Don’t repeat the subject: It was Maria who found the keys.
Don’t add ‘there’: the place is already the focus.
The pattern is It wasn’t until + time + that…
The negative of an it-cleft goes on ‘be’: It wasn’t the money…
A cleft question uses ‘be’: Was it your brother who called?
A wh-cleft needs ‘be’ before the focus: What I need is a holiday.
The verb ‘be’ is missing: What surprised me was his reaction.
A wh-cleft starts with ‘What’: What I need is a long holiday.
After ‘what she did was’, use the base verb: call, not called.
After ‘what he did was’, use the base verb: walk, not walked.
The what-clause is singular, so ‘was’ with the singular ‘reaction’.
For a place, use ‘Where’: Where we stayed in Paris was a tiny hotel by the river.
For the way something was done, use ‘How’: How she won the match was by staying calm.
A reverse wh-cleft uses ‘what’: A long holiday is what I need.
‘The problem’ is singular, so ‘is’.
‘Which’ isn’t used for people. Use ‘who’ or ‘that’: It was my sister who taught me to swim.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, which linking word, multiple choice and spot-the-mistake. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: It was Tom {{blank}} fixed the broken printer.
items.explain: Focus on a person who did the action: It was Tom who / that fixed it.
items.wrongNote: Use ‘who’ or ‘that’ after a person in an it-cleft.

items.sentText: What he did was {{blank}} to everyone.
items.explain: After ‘what he did was’ use the base verb, or to + base verb.
items.wrongNote: Use the base verb after ‘what… did was’: apologise, not apologised.

items.sentText: It wasn’t {{blank}} after dinner that she told us.
items.explain: The pattern is It wasn’t until + time + that + clause.

items.sentText: {{blank}} annoys me most is the constant noise.
items.explain: A wh-cleft starts with ‘What’ + clause + be + focus.

items.text: It was last summer {{blank}} we first visited Lisbon.
wrongReasons: ‘Who’ is for people, but ‘last summer’ is a time.
‘What’ doesn’t link a time focus to the clause.
‘Which’ is too formal and not used after a time focus.
items.explain: After a time in focus, the linking word is ‘that’.

items.text: It is our manager {{blank}} makes the final decision.
wrongReasons: ‘What’ can’t follow a person focus.
‘Where’ is for places.
‘Whose’ shows possession, which isn’t the meaning here.
items.explain: After a person who does the action, use ‘who’ (or ‘that’).

items.text: The sad fact is {{blank}} many young people never vote.
wrongReasons: ‘What’ can’t follow ‘the sad fact is’.
‘Who’ would need a person as the focus.
‘Where’ would need a place as the focus.
items.explain: A thing-cleft with ‘fact’ is followed by a that-clause.

items.text: A cold drink is {{blank}} I need right now.
wrongReasons: ‘That’ can’t introduce a reverse wh-cleft.
‘Who’ is for people, but a cold drink is a thing.
‘Where’ is for places, but a cold drink is a thing.
items.explain: A reverse wh-cleft has the structure focus + is + what + clause.

items.text: It {{blank}} the teacher who made the mistake, it was the student.
wrongReasons: ‘Weren’t’ doesn’t agree with ‘it’.
‘Didn’t’ can’t be followed by ‘the teacher who’.
‘Hadn’t’ can’t be followed by ‘the teacher who’.
items.explain: The negative goes on ‘be’, and the past ‘made’ needs ‘wasn’t’.

items.text: What she did {{blank}} close the door quietly.
wrongReasons: ‘Were’ doesn’t agree with the singular ‘what she did’.
‘Did’ can’t link the clause and the focus.
‘Has’ can’t link the clause and the focus.
items.explain: The linking verb is ‘be’, and ‘did’ shows the past: was.

choices: It were Maria who called me.
It was Maria who she called me.
It was Maria who called me.
wrongReasons: An it-cleft needs ‘it’.
‘It’ is singular, so ‘were’ is wrong.
The subject can’t be repeated.

choices: What she left remains a mystery.
Why she left remains a mystery.
Why she left it remains a mystery.
Why she left are a mystery.
wrongReasons: ‘What she left’ has a different meaning.
You can’t add ‘it’ after the clause.
‘Are’ doesn’t agree with the singular clause.

items.message: An it-cleft needs ‘it’: It was Maria who found the keys.
‘It’ is singular: It was the students who complained.
After ‘what he did was’, use the base verb.
‘Who’ is for people. For a thing use ‘that’.
